## Overview

**Kha'Thuun, The Witness from Beyond** — a Mind Flayer whose mind reached beyond the limits of mortal understanding, delving into truths that no living being was ever meant to witness. Among the Five Great Generals, he served as the Scourge's supreme intelligence — never commanding armies directly, but ensuring that every campaign began with overwhelming informational superiority. He was never defeated; like Vaessra before him, he simply vanished from history.

---

## Species

Mind Flayer (Illithid). Among the countless horrors that marched beneath the banners of the Scourge, few were as alien or as profoundly unsettling as the Illithids — psionic tyrants and interdimensional voyagers who viewed sentient life not as equals but as resources to be harvested, studied, and ultimately dominated. While many Mind Flayers sought knowledge to elevate their own colonies, Kha'Thuun pursued something far greater. By the time the Scourge rose to power, Kha'Thuun had already become the greatest psionic mind within its ranks.

---

## Title

**The Witness from Beyond.** No title carried by the Great Generals inspired more speculation than that of Kha'Thuun. Throughout the centuries, scholars, priests, and kings debated its meaning without ever reaching a consensus. Some believed he had gazed beyond the boundaries of reality itself, witnessing truths no mortal mind could survive. Others claimed he possessed memories belonging to forgotten worlds or ancient civilizations long erased from existence. None could prove these theories, yet one fact remained undeniable: Kha'Thuun always seemed to know what others believed impossible to know.

---

## Appearance

Kha'Thuun possessed the unmistakable form of an Illithid, though his presence transcended that of his kin. Towering above most mortals with an unnaturally slender frame, he moved with an almost effortless grace, as though untouched by the physical world around him. His pale violet skin appeared almost translucent beneath layers of intricately woven black robes embroidered with silver patterns resembling constellations and impossible geometric forms. Four long tentacles hung motionless from his face, rarely twitching unless he spoke directly into another creature's mind. His great obsidian eyes reflected neither emotion nor intent, giving the unsettling impression that they were not looking at those before him, but through them. Unlike the other Great Generals, Kha'Thuun carried no weapon, no armor, and no visible symbol of authority. His mind alone was more dangerous than any blade ever forged.

---

## Personality

Kha'Thuun rarely spoke aloud — not because he was silent by nature, but because spoken language seemed painfully primitive compared to thought itself. Detached from ordinary emotion, he regarded nearly every creature as an object of observation rather than an individual worthy of judgment.

Unlike Khar'Zul, whose mind revolved around conquest, or Vaessra, who understood the hearts of mortals, Kha'Thuun sought only understanding. He watched civilizations rise and collapse with the same quiet curiosity a scholar might reserve for an experiment. Victory, defeat, loyalty, and betrayal held little emotional significance to him; they were simply outcomes to be studied. Conversations with him often left others deeply unsettled, for he possessed an uncanny habit of answering questions before they were spoken or referencing memories that had never been shared.

---

## Philosophy

To Kha'Thuun, knowledge was the only true form of power. Strength could be overcome; kingdoms would inevitably crumble; even immortality could be undone — but knowledge endured beyond all of them. Every war was won long before the first sword was drawn, not through courage or numbers, but through understanding. Those who possessed complete knowledge could shape the future itself, while those who acted in ignorance merely fulfilled destinies they could not perceive. Mortals believed themselves free to choose their path, yet Kha'Thuun saw every decision as another predictable consequence of information they lacked. His obsession was never domination for its own sake — it was the endless pursuit of truth, no matter how incomprehensible or horrifying that truth might become.

---

## Military Command — The Black Legion

Unlike the other Great Generals, Kha'Thuun almost never commanded armies directly. His role within the Scourge was not to lead charges or besiege cities, but to ensure that every campaign began with overwhelming informational superiority.

While the Black Legion gathered intelligence across the world, Kha'Thuun pieced together countless fragments into a complete understanding of his enemies. He identified weaknesses in kingdoms before their rulers recognized them, uncovered hidden alliances before they were formed, and predicted military movements with astonishing precision. By the time Khar'Zul planned a campaign, Voragos selected his target, or Vaessra entered diplomatic negotiations, Kha'Thuun had already revealed every secret worth knowing. To the Scourge, knowledge was not merely support for war — it was the foundation upon which every victory was built.

Kha'Thuun commanded the Black Legion, the smallest yet arguably most indispensable force within the Scourge. Unlike the vast military formations of the other Great Generals, the Black Legion was composed of highly specialized operatives whose value lay not in overwhelming strength but in the information they could obtain. Mind Flayers, Intellect Devourers, psionic aberrations, and other creatures gifted with extraordinary mental abilities formed its core, travelling far beyond the front lines in search of forgotten libraries, ancient relics, hidden civilizations, and military intelligence. Entire campaigns depended upon the discoveries made by the Black Legion. To Kha'Thuun, a single forgotten truth was often worth more than ten thousand soldiers.

---

## Rise Through the Scourge

Unlike the other Great Generals, Kha'Thuun never sought influence through conquest, destruction, or political ambition. His rise was almost imperceptible. As the Scourge expanded across the world, impossible victories accumulated with increasing frequency. Kingdoms found their hidden supply routes exposed. Secret fortifications were bypassed with uncanny accuracy. Alliances collapsed before they could even unite against the enemy. Again and again, these triumphs traced back to knowledge that should never have been available.

Eventually even the leaders of the Scourge came to recognize that every successful campaign relied upon the same unseen architect. When Kha'Thuun was elevated to the rank of Great General, it was not because he inspired armies or sought authority, but because the Scourge had come to understand a simple truth: every war was easier to win when one side already knew everything.

---

## Reputation

Among the people of the world, Kha'Thuun inspired a uniquely unsettling fear. Unlike Voragos, whose shadow darkened the skies, or Xerathul, whose undead marched openly across battlefields, Kha'Thuun often remained unseen throughout entire campaigns. Yet kings trusted their advisors less; generals abandoned carefully prepared strategies; and scholars destroyed their own writings rather than risk them falling into unknown hands. It became widely believed that no secret remained hidden forever, for somewhere beyond the reach of mortal understanding, the Witness from Beyond was already watching. Even within the Scourge, the other Great Generals rarely questioned how Kha'Thuun obtained his knowledge — they simply accepted that whenever he spoke, he was almost always correct.

---

## Fate

Unlike Voragos, Xerathul, and Khar'Zul, Kha'Thuun was never defeated. As the Scourge gradually lost ground across the world, the Witness from Beyond disappeared without warning, leaving behind neither explanation nor trace of his departure.

No final battle was ever recorded; no body recovered; no reliable witness could account for his fate. Some believed he had foreseen the inevitable decline of the Scourge centuries before it occurred and simply departed once its purpose had been fulfilled. Others whispered that his search for forbidden knowledge had led him beyond the boundaries of the mortal world altogether. Whatever the truth may be, history records only one certainty: like Vaessra before him, Kha'Thuun vanished from history, and with him disappeared countless secrets that perhaps were never meant to be known.
